```{r setup}
#| include: false
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(dplyr); library(tidyr); library(sf); library(ggplot2); library(glue)
  library(patchwork); library(knitr); library(scales); library(purrr); library(readr)
  library(stringr); library(ggrepel)
})
source("R/00_config.R"); source("R/helpers.R"); source("R/huff_core.R")
invisible(Sys.setlocale("LC_CTYPE", "en_US.UTF-8"))  # R runs in the C locale here; keeps R² and × intact

# The helpers read PAL at call time, so overriding it converts every figure in
# the deck to the dark palette without touching a plot definition.
PAL <- modifyList(PAL, list(
  ink = "#F4E7DF", ground = "#2B1512", rule = "#593029", muted = "#C3A79B",
  land = "#4A2822", land_line = "#2B1512", null = "#4A2A24",
  accent = "#5FB3BC", accent_lt = "#2F6E75", loss = "#F0864B", loss_lt = "#9E4A40",
  div = c("#F0864B", "#D08A6C", "#A98C82", "#8C8580", "#7FA3A6", "#5FB3BC", "#A9DCE0")))

origins  <- read_rds(file.path(DER, "origins.rds"))
stations <- read_rds(file.path(DER, "stations.rds"))
cal      <- read_rds(file.path(DER, "calibration.rds"))
scn      <- read_rds(file.path(DER, "scenario.rds"))
va       <- read_rds(file.path(DER, "value_added.rds"))
r5       <- read_rds(file.path(DER, "scenario_r5.rds"))
subzone  <- st_read(F_SUBZONE, quiet = TRUE) |> st_transform(STUDY_CRS) |>
  st_make_valid() |> select(SUBZONE_N, PLN_AREA_N, REGION_N)
stn <- cal$stn; th <- cal$fits[[cal$best]]$theta; res <- scn$res
ex <- filter(stations, existing); n_fit <- length(cal$cal_idx)
cv_of <- function(m, col) cal$cv[[col]][cal$cv$model == m]
pct <- function(x) percent(x, accuracy = 1); num <- function(x, a = 1) comma(x, accuracy = a)
lines_sf <- function(s) s |> mutate(kind = case_when(new & str_detect(lines_2030, "JRL") ~ "Jurong Region Line",
                                                     new & str_detect(lines_2030, "CRL") ~ "Cross Island Line",
                                                     TRUE ~ "Existing"))
mapt <- function(base = 13, crop = TRUE) list(if (crop) sg_crop(stations) else coord_sf(expand = FALSE, datum = NA),
                                             theme_map(base_size = base))
kf <- function(...) {
  items <- list(...)
  cat('<div class="kf">')
  for (it in items) cat(sprintf('<div><div class="n">%s</div><div class="l">%s</div></div>', it[[1]], it[[2]]))
  cat('</div>')
}
nn <- res |> filter(new) |> arrange(-pred_2030)
q10 <- quantile(stn$tap_am[cal$cal_idx], 0.1)
low <- nn |> filter(pred_2030 < q10)
```

## Contents {.smaller}

:::

2. Clearing the land mines

## 1. The question, the place and the data

```{r}
#| output: asis
kf(list(num(nrow(origins)), "HDB residential blocks"),
   list(paste0(round(sum(origins$du) / 1e6, 2), "M"), "dwelling units"),
   list(sum(stations$existing), "stations today"),
   list(sum(stations$new), "new by 2030"))
```

::: {.split}
::: {.col}
```{r sl-map}
#| fig-height: 4.6
#| fig-width: 7.2
s_all <- lines_sf(stations)
ggplot() + base_land(subzone) +
  geom_sf(data = origins, aes(size = du), colour = "#B79A8E", alpha = 0.35, stroke = 0) +
  geom_sf(data = filter(s_all, kind == "Existing"), shape = 21, fill = PAL$ground, colour = PAL$ink, size = 1.1, stroke = 0.4) +
  geom_sf(data = filter(s_all, kind != "Existing"), aes(fill = kind), shape = 21, colour = PAL$ground, size = 2.4, stroke = 0.4) +
  scale_size_area(max_size = 1.5, guide = "none") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Jurong Region Line" = LINE_COLS[["JRL"]], "Cross Island Line" = LINE_COLS[["CRL"]]), name = NULL) +
  mapt(11)
```
:::
::: {.note}
**How many people will board at each new JRL and CRL station, and which stations
will they come from?** Stations open late when their riders are not there yet: Hume
waited ten years, Buangkok three.

**What is modelled.** Weekday tap-ins from 06:00 to 09:00, August to October 2026,
from LTA DataMall. In the morning most trips start at home, so a station's
boardings come from the housing around it.

**Market potential.** Dwelling units in every HDB block, the housing of about four
in five residents.

*Grey dots are HDB blocks, sized by dwelling units; teal and green are the new lines.*
:::
:::

## 2. Clearing the land mines

::: {.split .even .roomy}
::: {.col}
[What the data hid]{.colhead}

**The two HDB files share no key.** One street code per street made it possible: one
block per street geocoded with OneMap gave a crosswalk that places all 10,817
residential blocks.

**LTA's station layer includes ghost stations.** Bukit Brown, Mount Pleasant, Marina
South and Founders' Memorial are built and board nobody. The passenger data, not the
station layer, decides what exists.

**Circle Line stage 6 is already open.** Keppel, Cantonment and Prince Edward Road
are listed as planned but carry passengers; they join today's network.
:::
::: {.note}
[What the model can be judged on]{.colhead}

**`r sum(ex$du_1km < CAL_MIN_DU_1KM)` stations have almost no HDB housing within 1 km:**
private estates (Newton, Stevens), industry (Tuas), the airport and the central area.
Newton and Kranji board over 200,000 people a month in the morning with no HDB block
within a kilometre.

They stay in every choice set, competing for riders, but the model is fitted on the
other **`r n_fit`**. The data agree: the fitted stations board
`r round(with(st_drop_geometry(stn)[cal$cal_idx, ], sum(tap_am) / sum(tapout_am)), 1)` morning tap-ins per
tap-out, the excluded ones `r round(with(st_drop_geometry(stn)[-cal$cal_idx, ], sum(tap_am) / sum(tapout_am)), 1)`.
:::
:::

## 3. The model

::: {.split}
::: {.col}
$$
P_{ij} = \frac{A_j\, d_{ij}^{\lambda}}{\sum_{l \in C_i} A_l\, d_{il}^{\lambda}}
\qquad
\hat T_j = k \sum_i DU_i\, P_{ij}
$$

A resident of block $i$ boards at station $j$ with a probability that rises with the
station's attractiveness $A_j$ and falls with distance. Each station's predicted
boardings are the dwelling units it draws, times one trip rate $k$.

$A_j$ is multiplicative in lines served, bus stops and points of interest within
400 m, and whether the station is LRT-only, as in an MCI model.
:::
::: {.note}
**Choice set.** Every station within 3 km of a block, and at least its three
nearest.

**Calibration.** Parameters minimise the squared error of *log* boardings, so a 20%
miss costs the same at a small station as a large one.

**Validation.** 10-fold cross-validation over stations: hidden stations stay in
every choice set and only their ridership is withheld, which is the position of a
new station.

**Checked** against `MCI::huff.shares()`: the shares agree to the 15th decimal place.
:::
:::

## 4. What makes a station attractive

```{r}
#| output: asis
kf(list(pct(cv_of("M0", "R2_log")), "textbook Huff, cross-validated R²"),
   list(pct(cv_of("M3", "R2_log")), "full model, cross-validated R²"),
   list(sprintf("%.2f", cv_of("M3", "spearman")), "rank correlation"),
   list(paste0(round(cv_of("M3", "MdAPE_pct")), "%"), "median miss"))
```

::: {.split}
::: {.col}
```{r sl-params}
#| fig-height: 3.2
#| fig-width: 6.4
lab_terms <- c(lambda = "Distance exponent", n_lines = "Lines served", bus_stops = "Bus stops",
               poi = "Points of interest", lrt_only = "LRT-only")
p <- tibble(term = names(th), estimate = th) |> left_join(cal$ci, by = "term") |>
  mutate(term = factor(lab_terms[term], rev(lab_terms)))
ggplot(p, aes(estimate, term)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = PAL$muted, linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_errorbarh(aes(xmin = lo, xmax = hi), height = 0, colour = PAL$accent, linewidth = 0.9) +
  geom_point(colour = PAL$accent, size = 2.6) +
  labs(x = "Estimate with 95% bootstrap interval", y = NULL) + theme_ex03(13, grid = "x")
```
:::
::: {.note}
**A second line multiplies a station's pull by `r round((3/2)^th[["n_lines"]], 1)`.** People
walk further to an interchange because it saves a transfer later.

**Ten times the shops and services: ×`r round(10^th[["poi"]], 1)`.** Activity adds a smaller pull.

**An LRT-only station has `r pct(exp(th[["lrt_only"]]))` of the pull** of an equivalent
MRT station.

**Distance decays with exponent `r round(th[["lambda"]], 2)`:** doubling the distance cuts the pull by
×`r round(2^-th[["lambda"]], 1)`. Bus stops add nothing once the rest is in.
:::
:::

## 5. Where the model misses

::: {.split}
::: {.col}
```{r sl-resid}
#| fig-height: 4.8
#| fig-width: 7.2
d <- stn[cal$cal_idx, ]
ggplot() + base_land(subzone) +
  geom_sf(data = d, aes(fill = pmax(pmin(resid_log, 1.2), -1.2)), shape = 21, size = 3.4, colour = PAL$ground, stroke = 0.3) +
  scale_fill_gradientn(colours = PAL$div, limits = c(-1.2, 1.2), name = "log(observed / predicted)") +
  mapt(11)
```
:::
::: {.note}
**The misses cluster.** Moran's I of the residuals is
`r round(cal$moran_resid$estimate[1], 2)` (p < 0.001).

**Under-predicted (teal):** city-fringe stations that mix HDB with private housing,
such as Novena, Great World, Katong Park and Beauty World. The extra riders live in
homes the model cannot see.

**Over-predicted (orange):** stations opened recently (Keppel, 2026) and stations
whose blocks mostly walk to a stronger neighbour (Bendemeer, Labrador Park).

One distance exponent for the whole island is the obvious suspect; slide 9 tests it.
:::
:::

## 6. Ridership at the new stations

::: {.split}
::: {.col}
```{r sl-new}
#| fig-height: 5.4
#| fig-width: 6.6
d <- nn |> mutate(name = reorder(name, pred_2030), line = ifelse(line_new == "JRL", "JRL", "CRL"))
ggplot(d, aes(pred_2030, name)) +
  annotate("rect", xmin = q10, xmax = quantile(stn$tap_am[cal$cal_idx], 0.5), ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf, fill = PAL$land) +
  geom_errorbarh(aes(xmin = pred_2030_lo, xmax = pred_2030_hi, colour = line), height = 0, linewidth = 0.7) +
  geom_point(aes(colour = line), size = 2) +
  scale_x_log10(labels = label_comma()) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(JRL = LINE_COLS[["JRL"]], CRL = LINE_COLS[["CRL"]]), name = NULL) +
  labs(x = "Predicted morning boardings per month (log scale)", y = NULL) +
  theme_ex03(12, grid = "x")
```
:::
::: {.note}
**The strong stations sit in housing with no station today.** Tengah Plantation
(`r num(nn$pred_2030[nn$name == "Tengah Plantation"], 1000)` a month), Serangoon North
(`r num(nn$pred_2030[nn$name == "Serangoon North"], 1000)`) and Pasir Ris East
(`r num(nn$pred_2030[nn$name == "Pasir Ris East"], 1000)`).

**`r nrow(low)` fall below today's 10th percentile:** `r paste(low$name, collapse = ", ")`.
Few homes surround them. In a home-based model they are the ghost-station risk; their
case rests on jobs and campuses this model cannot see.

*Shaded: today's fitted stations, 10th to 50th percentile. Bars: 95% bootstrap intervals.*
:::
:::

## 7. Who the new lines take riders from

::: {.split}
::: {.col}
```{r sl-impact}
#| fig-height: 4.8
#| fig-width: 7.2
d <- stations |> select(name) |> left_join(res, by = "name")
ggplot() + base_land(subzone) +
  geom_sf(data = filter(d, existing, !is.na(change_pct)),
          aes(fill = pmax(change_pct, -0.6), size = pred_now), shape = 21, colour = PAL$ground, stroke = 0.25) +
  geom_sf(data = filter(d, new), aes(colour = line_new), shape = 18, size = 2.6) +
  scale_fill_gradientn(colours = c(PAL$loss, "#D9926E", "#A8796C", "#8C8079"), limits = c(-0.6, 0.05),
                       labels = label_percent(), name = "Change") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(JRL = LINE_COLS[["JRL"]], CRL = LINE_COLS[["CRL"]]), name = NULL) +
  scale_size_area(max_size = 6, guide = "none") + mapt(11)
```
:::
::: {.note}
```{r}
#| output: asis
top <- res |> filter(existing) |> arrange(change) |> head(5)
cat(paste0("**", top$name, "** ", pct(top$change_pct), " (", num(top$change, 1000), " a month)", collapse = "<br>"))
```

The losses fall where the new lines run *between* existing stations. The JRL's
Jurong West branch takes the estates that walk to Chinese Garden, Lakeside and
Pioneer today; the Tengah stations take riders from Bukit Batok and Bukit Gombak.

For the operator this is relief: these are among the busiest morning stations on the
East-West and North-South lines.
:::
:::

## 8. Market areas in the west

```{r sl-market}
#| fig-height: 4.7
#| fig-width: 11.5
west <- st_as_sfc(st_bbox(c(xmin = 11000, xmax = 23500, ymin = 31000, ymax = 42500), crs = st_crs(STUDY_CRS)))
o_w <- origins |> st_filter(west) |> left_join(scn$dom, by = "origin_id")
top <- union(names(sort(table(o_w$station_now), decreasing = TRUE))[1:12], names(sort(table(o_w$station_2030), decreasing = TRUE))[1:14])
pal_st <- setNames(rep_len(c("#5FB3BC", "#F0864B", "#8FA8D6", "#E3B566", "#7CC38B", "#C79BD0", "#4C9AB0", "#E39A7E",
                             "#B5C46A", "#D1A06A", "#6FB3A4", "#D08AA0", "#8E9CD0", "#D9B84E", "#A68FD0", "#6DBA87"), length(top)), top)
stn_w <- st_filter(lines_sf(stations), west)
o_w <- o_w |> mutate(change = case_when(to_new ~ "Switches to a new station",
                                       switched ~ "Switches to another existing station",
                                       TRUE ~ "Keeps its station"))
p_now <- ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = st_crop(subzone, west), fill = PAL$land, colour = PAL$land_line, linewidth = 0.15) +
  geom_sf(data = o_w, aes(colour = ifelse(station_now %in% top, station_now, "other")), size = 0.8) +
  geom_sf(data = filter(stn_w, existing), shape = 21, size = 1.8, colour = PAL$ink, fill = PAL$ground) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(pal_st, other = PAL$null), guide = "none") +
  labs(title = "Today") + mapt(12, crop = FALSE) +
  theme(plot.background = element_rect(fill = NA, colour = NA), plot.title = element_text(colour = PAL$ink))
p_30 <- ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = st_crop(subzone, west), fill = PAL$land, colour = PAL$land_line, linewidth = 0.15) +
  geom_sf(data = o_w, aes(colour = change), size = 0.8) +
  geom_sf(data = filter(stn_w, existing), shape = 21, size = 1.8, colour = PAL$ink, fill = PAL$ground) +
  geom_sf(data = filter(stn_w, !existing), aes(fill = kind), shape = 23, size = 2.4, colour = PAL$ink) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("Switches to a new station" = LINE_COLS[["JRL"]],
                                 "Switches to another existing station" = PAL$loss,
                                 "Keeps its station" = PAL$null), name = NULL) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Jurong Region Line" = LINE_COLS[["JRL"]], "Cross Island Line" = LINE_COLS[["CRL"]]), guide = "none") +
  guides(colour = guide_legend(nrow = 2, override.aes = list(size = 3))) +
  labs(title = "2030, with the JRL") + mapt(12, crop = FALSE) +
  theme(plot.background = element_rect(fill = NA, colour = NA), plot.title = element_text(colour = PAL$ink))
(p_now + p_30) & theme(plot.background = element_rect(fill = NA, colour = NA))
```

::: {.subhead}
Left: each HDB block coloured by the station that draws most of its residents today.
Right: the blocks whose main station changes in 2030. `r num(sum(scn$dom$switched))` blocks change
across the island, `r num(sum(scn$dom$to_new))` of them to a new station. Tengah, today on the edge of
Bukit Batok's and Choa Chu Kang's catchments, gets stations of its own.
:::

## 9. Does distance decay differ across the island?

::: {.split}
::: {.col}
```{r sl-va}
#| fig-height: 3.6
#| fig-width: 6.4
{
  lr <- va$lambda_region |> mutate(region = str_to_title(sub(" REGION", "", region)))
  ggplot(lr, aes(lambda, reorder(region, lambda))) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = th[["lambda"]], linetype = 2, colour = PAL$muted, linewidth = 0.3) +
    geom_errorbarh(aes(xmin = lo, xmax = hi), height = 0, colour = PAL$accent, linewidth = 0.9) +
    geom_point(colour = PAL$accent, size = 2.6) +
    labs(x = "Distance exponent by region of the home block", y = NULL) + theme_ex03(13, grid = "x")
}
```
:::
::: {.note}
```{r}
#| include: false
lr5 <- va$lambda_region |> mutate(region = str_to_title(sub(" REGION", "", region)))
lrv <- function(r, col = "lambda") round(lr5[[col]][lr5$region == r], 1)
```

**One exponent per region of the home block.** North-East (`r lrv("North-East")`) and
West (`r lrv("West")`) residents are about twice as distance-sensitive as Central ones
(`r lrv("Central")`). Newer towns are built around their own stop; central residents can
choose among several stations.

**It predicts held-out stations better:** R² `r round(va$cv$R2_log[va$cv$model == "R5"], 2)` against
`r round(cv_of("M3", "R2_log"), 2)`. Exponential decay does worse (`r round(va$cv$R2_log[va$cv$model == "EXP"], 2)`).

**The 2030 conclusions hold.** New stations rank the same (ρ = `r round(r5$summ$rho_new, 2)`).
Only the western interchanges change: Jurong East loses
`r pct(-r5$cmp$change_pct_r5[r5$cmp$name == "Jurong East"])` instead of
`r pct(-r5$cmp$change_pct[r5$cmp$name == "Jurong East"])`.

*East and North intervals are too wide to read.*
:::
:::

## 10. What this means for planning, and what it cannot say

::: {.split .even .roomy}
::: {.col}
[For planners and operators]{.colhead}

**Open the residential JRL stations with the line.** Tengah Plantation, Choa Chu
Kang West and the Jurong West branch will board like today's busy heartland
stations.

**Judge the destination stations on jobs, not homes.** Aviation Park, Jurong Pier,
Jurong Hill and Loyang will look empty in a home-based morning model; time their
opening to the employment around them.

**Redraw the Jurong West and Bukit Batok feeder buses** towards the new stations.
:::
::: {.note}
[What it cannot say]{.colhead}

**Private housing is invisible** to it, which is why private-estate stations were
left out of the fit.

**It predicts home-based morning boardings,** not total ridership; destination
stations need a model with employment as the attraction.

**Straight-line distance** stands in for the walk and the feeder bus, and new
stations are measured on today's surroundings, so their predictions are a floor.

*The brief's "public-safety" and "peace-keeping" implications are a carry-over from
Take-home 2 and do not apply to rail ridership.*
:::
:::
